key_insight: Extending BK19 with asymptotically derived switches enables quasi-geostrophic dynamics within the same discretization used for compressible, pseudo-incompressible, and hydrostatic flow.
engineering_relevance: A unified solver can represent fast compressible motion and slow, balanced atmospheric dynamics without switching numerical frameworks.
method: Analyze the fully discrete scheme at synoptic scales in the small-Rossby-number limit.
Construct a consistent staggered-grid curl operator and recover the QG pressure Poisson equation.
Add switches for the pressure equation and prognostic versus geostrophically diagnosed horizontal momenta.
evidence_signal: Two idealized vortex tests assess QG vortex stability and show convergence of the compressible solver toward balanced QG dynamics as the Rossby number decreases.
watch_item: Validation is limited to two idealized vortex cases; performance in complex atmospheric flows is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Access to the quasi-geostrophic model from within the BK19 compressible flow solver
